title: Heuristic tuner UI playbook — batching/cache/quantize editor (draft)
content:
Goal: Draft a lightweight in-console editor for 'heuristic tuners' — named presets that combine batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization recommendations with rollout rules and validation pipelines. This doc captures wireframe notes, interaction flows, backlog grooming, and acceptance criteria for an initial MVP.

Overview / product rationale:
- Customers repeatedly ask for opinionated, testable performance toggles rather than raw knobs. The heuristic-tuner is an authorable preset: a small declarative bundle of (batching policy, cache scope, quantize profile, target SLOs, canary policy).
- It should be straightforward to create, preview on sample traffic, and stage as a rollout (canary => ramp => full). Observability hooks must show estimated cost delta and latency distribution before/after.

Primary user stories:
1) As an ML engineer, I want to author a tuner that reduces per-token cost for an e-commerce chat workload while preserving <= 10% generation-quality delta.
2) As a platform engineer, I want to preview tuner effects on synthetic traces and production-sampled requests in a sandbox before enabling in Dedicated environments.
3) As a product owner, I want to rollback or fallback automatically if 95th percentile latency exceeds an SLO or quality regressions are detected.

Wireframe notes (high level panels):
- Left rail: tuner list + quick filters (active, draft, by model family, by tag). Inline badges: est cost delta, risk score.
- Main canvas split top/bottom:
  - Top: editor canvas (name, description, base model target, SLO targets, confidence threshold for quality checks).
  - Middle: policy builder (drag/choose components): batching block, cache block, quantization block, routing/fallback block.
  - Each block expands into a right-side detail panel for fine-grained settings.
  - Bottom: Preview & validation tabbed view: "Synthetic Preview", "Sampling Preview", "Validation Results".
- Right rail: quick simulation controls (sample traffic selector, sequence-length distribution, parallel QPS slider), quick-run button, and microcopy tips.

Editor interactions (sketch of flow):
- Create new tuner -> choose a template or blank. Templates: latency-first, cost-first, conservative-cache, aggressive-quant.
- In policy builder, user can order batching vs cache precedence. UI enforces that batching policy applies at runtime; cache is prefix-based and can be marked global vs route-scoped.
- Quantization block shows compatible quant levels (int8, int4 simulated), with warnings for model incompatibility.
- Routing block defines fallback chains: primary tuned model -> fallback to base model -> fallback region. Can set failure thresholds and timeouts.
- Save as draft, run preview, open validation pipeline. If preview run succeeds, enable canary rollout settings.

Preview & validation:
- Synthetic Preview: uses user-chosen sequence-length histogram and tokenization model to estimate latency/cost changes (simulation). Show token-level cost delta and expected 50/95/99 latency percentiles.
- Sampling Preview: run tuner on a small sampled subset of recent production requests (privacy scrubbed). Display side-by-side diffs: tokens, cost, latency, and a simple quality signal (e.g., perplexity delta or user-provided eval metric).
- Validation Results: structured pass/fail checks tied to quality thresholds. Shows regressions by prompt set and offers rewind button to edit tuner parameters.

Telemetry & observability to capture:
- EstCostDeltaPct, EstLatencyP95Delta, ValidationFailReasons (list, stringified), CanarySuccessRate, FallbackRate, CacheHitRate (route & global), BatchingAvgBatchSize.
- Surface the above metrics on tuner summary card; allow click-through to per-route traces.

Microcopy / inline help examples:
- For batching: "Increase batch size to improve throughput; watch tail latencies for short requests." 
- For caching: "Prefix caching stores KV for prompt prefixes; route-scoped caches are safer for multi-tenant models." 
- For quantization: "Lower-precision models reduce cost but may change output probabilities. Use validation to detect quality drift." 
- For rollouts: "Canary at 5% for 24h, then 25% for 48h if validation passes. Auto-fallback on 95th% latency breach > 200ms."

Backlog (groomed items, priorities, rough estimates):
- OPT-521: Tuner list UI + filters (owner: Liam) — 3d — must include cost delta badges and search. Priority: P0.
- OPT-522: Policy builder skeleton + component tiles (owner: Priya) — 5d — drag/drop baseline, persist JSON spec. Priority: P0.
- OPT-523: Simulator engine integration (owner: Noah) — 8d — run synthetic histogram simulations in background, show estimations. Priority: P0.
- OPT-524: Sampling preview pipeline (owner: Sofia) — 10d — privacy scrub + sampled replay with limited qps. Priority: P1 (needs infra gating).
- OPT-525: Validation rules engine + UI (owner: Asha) — 6d — allow plug-in rules and baseline comparisons. Priority: P0.
- OPT-526: Rollout workflows + automatic fallback wiring (owner: Platform Eng lead) — 7d — integrate with routing/rollouts system. Priority: P0.
- OPT-527: Telemetry dashboards + alerts (owner: SRE) — 4d — surface tuner metrics and set defaults.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Users can create a tuner with at least 3 components (batching, cache, quantize) and save as draft.
- Users can run Synthetic Preview and receive an estimation for cost and p95 latency within reasonable bounds of actual runs (simulation accuracy > 70% on test traces).
- Users can run a Sampling Preview against a sampled set and see side-by-side deltas for at least cost and p95 latency.
- Tuner cards show EstCostDeltaPct and EstLatencyP95Delta and link to validation results.
- Canary rollout with automatic fallback can be configured and triggers a rollback when configured thresholds are breached.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should tuner specs be YAML/JSON editable for power users? (pro: reproducibility; con: surfaces complexity)
- How many templates to ship in MVP? Proposed: 4 (latency-first, cost-first, conservative, aggressive). Decision by product.
- What safety checks for quantization should be baked in (per-layer compatibility checks?)
- Is sampling preview available for Hosted customers or only Dedicated/Private due to privacy concerns?

Design notes for UX handoff:
- Use compact cards in list with color-coded risk (green/yellow/red). Risk computed from est cost delta and validation history.
- Provide one-click 'apply preset' from template tray to reduce time-to-first-preview.
- Keep the policy builder visually composable rather than form-heavy; allow expansion for advanced settings.

Prototype links and test plan:
- Figma: HeuristicTunerV2 (see linked_artifacts). Prototype flows: create -> simulate -> sample -> validate -> rollout.
- Usability plan: 5 quick sessions (internal ML engineers) to test: discoverability of templates, clarity of validation messages, and perceived trust in simulation numbers.

Next steps (immediate):
- Sync with platform infra to confirm sampling QPS limits and privacy scrub requirements (owner: Asha) — due 2024-11-12.
- Design first pass for tuner list and policy tiles (owner: Liam & Priya) — sync 2024-11-15.
- Spike for simulation accuracy measurement (owner: Noah) — 1 week spike to collect bench traces and compare sim vs real.

Notes from 2024-11-04 kickoff meeting:
- PMs: Asha, Priya. Engineering attendees: Liam, Noah. SRE: Cassie Ryder. Key constraint: do not expose aggressive-quant templates to self-serve free tier.
- Action: create Data Access request for sanitized sample set (DR-310) — blocked until privacy sign-off.

Revision history:
- 2024-11-05 initial draft (Asha)
- 2024-12-02 updated backlog and added telemetry fields (Noah)
- 2025-01-18 added acceptance criteria and clarified sampling preview scope (Asha)

"Notes to self" (working thoughts):
- Consider a compact CLI for advanced teams that allows bulk authoring of tuners (export/import JSON).
- Keep the templating system pluggable so Solutions Engineering can ship customer-specific templates.
- Evaluate whether cost delta should use live token pricing or a standardized estimated price point for comparability.

End of doc.
